e: AWS Secrets Manager stores the credentials securely, the application loads them at runtime (a small code change), and Secrets Manager rotation (with a Lambda rotation function it provides for RDS MySQL) keeps the credentials fresh. KMS keys aren't credential stores, local storage is weaker, and Parameter Store has no native rotation.

A new S3 bucket with SSE-KMS using multi-Region keys and Cross-Region Replication, with the data loaded into it so that both existing and new data are encrypted and replicated, and serverless Athena querying the data with SQL, has the least overhead. CRR on an existing bucket doesn't replicate existing objects, and RDS isn't serverless Athena-style querying.

Uploaded images are used only twice a year, so Glacier Deep Archive is cheapest; premium users' generated images need frequent immediate access (S3 Standard), while non-premium users download only every 6 hours, so S3 Standard-IA is cheaper. One Zone-IA risks losing the uploaded images, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval delays downloads.

Each model needs about 1 GB of data loaded at startup and requests are asynchronous and bursty, so an SQS queue buffers requests and ECS services that scale on queue size handle bursts and scale down when idle. Lambda's limits and cold starts, and a load balancer for async batches, are poor fits.

A pilot-light style DR in a second Region (ALB and a minimal Auto Scaling group) with an Aurora global database keeps the data replicated, and Route 53 active-passive failover lets the infrastructure scale up within the 30-minute recovery time when needed. Active-active or restore-from-backup designs don't match, and a single Auto Scaling group can't span Regions.

The batch jobs can't be disrupted, so use On-Demand Instances rather than Spot. Data is accessed for 30 days in S3 Standard, then moved to Glacier Deep Archive, the cheapest tier, which suits 2-year retention (meeting its minimum duration), and expires after 2 years.

Single-digit latency calls for Direct Connect: establish the connection with a transit virtual interface to a Direct Connect gateway, and associate that gateway with the transit gateway attached to the VPCs, which is cost-effective and covers all the VPCs. VPN adds internet-based latency variability.

RDS Proxy maintains a pool of connections and, on failover, keeps application connections and routes to the new primary, reducing failover time and avoiding application timeouts. Read replicas, Performance Insights, or snapshot copies don't shorten failover.

Systems Manager State Manager associations can target the tagged RDS instances and run the AWS-managed start/stop automation runbooks on a schedule, with no custom code. CloudWatch alarms, Trusted Advisor, or custom Lambda functions need more to build and maintain.

With Requester Pays enabled, the marketing firm pays the request and data transfer costs for its downloads, so the company's data transfer costs are minimized. Replication, RAM, or Intelligent-Tiering would still cost the company or add expense.

An AWS WAF web ACL with rate-based rules on the ALB mitigates request-flood (layer 7) DDoS attacks with little effort. WAF can't be associated directly with Global Accelerator, and Lambda-updated network ACLs or an extra CloudFront layer add effort.

The AWS Glue DynamoDB export connector reads from a table export to S3 (point-in-time export), which doesn't consume the table's provisioned read capacity, so the daily metrics don't affect the website. Athena's connector, Redshift COPY, or Hive on EMR scan the live table and use read capacity.

SQS durably stores the jobs and keeps the components loosely coupled, and Auto Scaling based on the number of items in the queue (backlog per instance) adds and removes instances to process jobs in parallel. SNS doesn't store jobs durably, and CPU or network metrics don't reflect backlog.

ECS on Fargate runs the containerized, modular services without managing servers, RDS Multi-AZ keeps the structured relational schemas highly available, and S3 stores the product images. EC2-based EKS, DynamoDB, storing images in RDS, or Glacier Deep Archive increase effort or don't fit.

The data must be encrypted before it is stored in S3, which means client-side encryption in the application (using keys the company manages), not server-side options, which encrypt after S3 receives the data. S3 managed keys can't be used for client-side encryption.

EMR runtime roles give each job its own IAM role scoped to the AWS services that team needs, and workloads submitted with them don't use the instance profile, so they can't reach credentials through IMDS. Shared instance profiles, VPC endpoints, or disabling application-scoped roles don't isolate per-team access.

An SQS FIFO queue between the tiers provides exactly-once processing, durable storage so no data is lost, and quick processing. Standard queues can deliver duplicates, and API Gateway or synchronous Step Functions don't buffer durably.

Kinesis Data Streams ingests the streaming data, Amazon OpenSearch Service provides real-time search and its dashboards, and QuickSight can visualize it, an AWS-native streaming search design. The other combinations aren't built for real-time search of streams.

AWS App2Container containerizes existing .NET/ASP.NET applications, and deploying to ECS on Fargate removes server management while scaling on CloudWatch metrics, minimizing operational work. ECS on EC2 requires managing instances, and App Runner doesn't containerize apps or deploy to ECS/EKS.

AWS Secrets Manager is the managed service for storing and retrieving credentials such as usernames and passwords, and the BatchGetSecretValue API retrieves multiple secrets in one call, with CloudFormation and no extra service. Parameter Store lacks secrets features, and adding AWS Batch is unnecessary.

A CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as origin caches the 100 software files at edge locations near the servers worldwide, reducing download latency with little management, and signed URLs control access. CachingDisabled defeats the purpose, and replication or Transfer Acceleration add effort or suit uploads.

FSx for NetApp ONTAP Multi-AZ provides highly available, low-latency block storage over iSCSI that fails over across Availability Zones, so an active/standby Windows pair can use it with the least effort. EBS volumes are AZ-bound with no built-in cross-AZ replication, and FSx for Windows is file (SMB) storage.

The ALB security group must allow inbound HTTPS from the internet on port 443, outbound HTTPS to the web instances on port 443 for forwarded traffic, and outbound traffic to the instances on port 8443 for the health checks. Security groups are stateful, so no inbound rules from the instances are needed.

CloudFront requires its custom domain certificate to be an ACM public certificate in us-east-1, and an S3 bucket policy allowing CloudFront through origin access control (OAC) lets CloudFront upload to the private bucket in eu-west-1. Transfer Acceleration or S3 website endpoints aren't needed.

Athena can query Parquet files directly in S3 (including client-side KMS-encrypted objects through its CSE-KMS support), charges only per query, and partitioning by day prefix limits what's scanned, making it the cheapest for occasional SQL. S3 Select doesn't handle this encryption well, and Redshift or EMR cost more.
